title: br ready --json omits labels required by dispatch filtering
description:
Blocking discovery while implementing ab-hmw. In the pinned br binary, br ready --json omits the labels field even for an open ready bead labeled seat:operator, while br show <id> --json and br label list expose the label. This invalidates ab-hmw's stated assumption that ReadyBead can deserialize labels directly from ready output and would silently dispatch operator-seat work. The engine now mitigates this with a second filtered ready query, but the substrate serialization defect remains. Relevant engine functions are ReadyBead, parse_ready, and select_bead in src/lib.rs and cmd_run in src/main.rs. Suggested resolution: fix br ready JSON upstream to serialize labels and pin that version; remove the engine's extra membership query only after the fixed live contract is verified.

## File footprint

src/lib.rs, src/main.rs, tests/br_roundtrip.rs, plus the upstream br ready JSON serializer or dependency pin once located.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a fresh temporary tracker with br init --prefix it.
2. Create an open priority-0 bead and add seat:operator with br label add.
3. Run br ready --json and observe no labels key.
4. Run br show <id> --json and observe labels containing seat:operator.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The pinned br ready --json output includes labels for labeled ready beads and an empty or default representation for unlabeled beads.
- An upstream integration test locks that serializer contract.
- The real temp-workspace test in tests/br_roundtrip.rs remains green.
- Only then may cmd_run's filtered second ready query be removed, with unit and integration tests updated before implementation.
- Full suite, cargo clippy, and cargo fmt --check green.
notes: ab-hmw mitigates the omission in the engine by intersecting primary ready output with br ready --label seat:operator --json before selection. The substrate serialization defect remains open; removing the extra query requires a pinned br version whose ready JSON includes labels.
close_reason: Resolved by the substrate upgrade: br 0.3.2 emits the labels field in ready --json, verified on the live store (ab-72p itself listed with seat:operator). The engine's membership-query workaround is now removable — tracked as the unblocked follow-up bead.

title: abacus land: admission, enqueue, exception watch wiring
description:
ADR 0003 D2′/D6′/D9′/D12: abacus land [repo] — process wiring over the pure policy module (which this bead requires, along with capture_status). Add land to main()'s match and usage().

The cycle (Decision section of the ADR is the contract; read it first): startup eligibility probe (refuse a repo whose queue/required checks are absent — BEFORE any side effect); enumerate candidates (open lane/* PRs × closed beads — branch name is the selector, D4, no PR numbers persisted); per candidate serially: admission (throwaway UNPUSHED git worktree, fetch fresh, compose branch with the discovered default branch tip, run suite+clippy+fmt on the composition), park on red / route conflicts to the exception handler without enqueueing; enqueue via bare gh pr merge <branch> (no strategy flag); exception watch (poll queue state with an INJECTED delay seam — no real sleeps in tests): a dequeue triggers exactly one agent-resolution lane (herdr worktree open --branch <lane-branch>, then agent start + prompt; launch carries bead id, attempt marker, resolution framing per CONSTRAINTS findings 2-3; the LANE pushes its own commits — abacus never pushes), then re-admission → re-enqueue on green, park on anything else. --once processes the current candidate set and exits (the test entry point). Stateless: no state file anywhere; every start recomputes from gh + br.

Integration tests (tests/land.rs NEW, fake gh + fake br + fake herdr + REAL git, CI-portable; harness pattern at tests/br_roundtrip.rs:249-306). Teardown invariant in EVERY test: assert_no_forbidden_flags(&gh_log, &git_log) — gh argv never contains --admin (gh's documented queue bypass — the single most load-bearing line), --match-head-commit, -d/--delete-branch, update-branch, or ruleset/branch-protection-mutating gh api calls; git argv never contains push, --force, --force-with-lease, -f, -X ours, -X theirs, --strategy-option.

- T4 (+T41): happy admission, main ahead by one: composition happens in a throwaway worktree, local-leg commands appear in the log against it, exactly one enqueue follows, PR branch head SHA unchanged at exit. T41: run this fixture with default branch "trunk" — zero-cost fixture parameter proving no main hardcode.
- T5: fake clippy exits 1 on the composition → park comment with evidence, no enqueue, no push.
- T7 (composition freshness): main advances externally between two --once cycles → the second composition contains the new tip as a parent (a stale cached origin/main satisfies the weak form and validates a fiction — assert ancestry, not "two cycles ran").
- T12: two closed beads, one PR → exit 0, that PR enqueued, the PR-less bead is a normal skip.
- T15: dequeued PR whose single resolution attempt fails → evidence comment posted, NO enqueue ever follows, PR left open, fake br log contains NO write verb (update/close/label) — the negative halves ARE the assertion.
- T22: main and branch both append .beads/issues.jsonl; the admission worktree inherits merge.beads-jsonl.driver → composition resolves, enqueue proceeds, fake herdr log EMPTY (proves the highest-probability conflict class resolves without burning an agent lane).

- T50: Queued then Dequeued across two watch reads → exactly one worktree open + agent prompt; no second enqueue before the attempt terminates; injected poll delay.
- T51 (one-attempt bound, green branch): fake agent resolves, re-admission green → exactly one further enqueue; total agent dispatches across the cycle = 1.
- T52: across a full cycle abacus's own git argv contains no push at all, and no admission worktree survives at exit (git worktree list shows only the main tree).

title: Transient probe failure aborts the run before the never-engaged retry can fire
description:
Observed 2026-08-14 18:13, first dispatch on the upgraded substrate:
the lane settled instantly (lost-prompt race, third occurrence — the
ab-f5f retry is merged and live) but the outcome probe itself failed —
br show <bead> --json exited 7 with empty stderr, aborting abacus run
before the probe could classify NeverEngaged, so the f5f retry never
ran. The same command succeeded manually seconds later: a transient of
the known database-busy-during-index-setup class (jotted 2026-08-14 on
0.1.45, now observed on 0.3.2), plausibly the store's first index pass
after the JSONL rebuild. Composition gap: any transient br error at
probe time masks the retry machinery entirely.

Fix in cmd_run (src/main.rs): when the post-settle br show probe exits
non-zero, retry the probe once after a short delay (about two seconds)
before propagating the error; only a second consecutive failure aborts
the run. This composes with the existing NeverEngaged retry — a probe
that succeeds on its second attempt feeds the normal classification,
which can then trigger the f5f re-prompt as designed.

## File footprint

src/main.rs, tests/br_roundtrip.rs

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Dispatch a bead while the shared store is briefly busy (first access
   after a JSONL rebuild reproduces the window).
2. The settle returns, the probe's br show exits non-zero transiently,
   and abacus run exits 1 without classifying or retrying anything.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit test covers the probe-retry decision: first non-zero probe
  triggers exactly one delayed re-probe; a second failure propagates
  the original error shape.
- A probe that succeeds on retry feeds normal outcome classification,
  including the NeverEngaged re-prompt path.
- Full suite, clippy, fmt green within budget.
notes: TDD evidence: integration regression first failed with br show exit status 7 after one prompt, reproducing the reported abort. Unit retry-contract tests then failed to compile before the helper existed. After implementation, targeted unit tests passed 2/2 and the transient-probe integration test passed 1/1. title: Default-branch discovery fails on checkouts without refs/remotes/origin/HEAD, blocking every dispatch
description:
Observed 2026-08-15 ~13:55 UTC, first dispatch after installing the PR-21/PR-23 binary: abacus run exited 1 before selection with: abacus run: git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD failed (exit status: 128): fatal: ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD is not a symbolic ref.

Cause: the D14 default-branch discovery (added in PR 21, discovery call site in cmd_run, src/main.rs) assumes refs/remotes/origin/HEAD exists. That ref is created by git clone only — a checkout built with git init + git remote add never has it, and a checkout can also lose or carry a stale one across a remote URL change (this checkout's origin was re-pointed to the org repository the same day). The failure precedes selection, so it blocks EVERY dispatch on an affected checkout — run, and by construction drain.

Workaround applied to the operator checkout, which resolves the immediate block: git remote set-head origin -a (sets origin/HEAD from the remote's advertised HEAD). Any other affected checkout needs the same until fixed.

Fix in the discovery call site (keep discovery out of the pure prompt function per D14): when git symbolic-ref exits non-zero, fall back to resolving the remote's advertised default — git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD (parse the "ref: refs/heads/<name> HEAD" line) — and optionally repair the local ref with git remote set-head origin -a for subsequent runs. Only if both paths fail should the dispatch abort, with an error naming both attempts.

## File footprint

src/main.rs, tests/br_roundtrip.rs

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a scratch repo: git init, add a commit, git remote add origin <any real remote>, git fetch origin (note: no origin/HEAD is created).
2. Run abacus run against it (or observe the operator-checkout instance above).
3. The run exits 1 at discovery, before selection, with the symbolic-ref 128 error.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit or integration test covers the discovery fallback: a fixture checkout WITHOUT refs/remotes/origin/HEAD still resolves the default branch (extend the PR-21 real-git fixture pattern in tests/br_roundtrip.rs; the existing origin/HEAD-present case must keep passing).
- A checkout with neither resolvable path produces a single clear error naming both attempted mechanisms.
- Full suite, clippy -D warnings, fmt --check green.

title: abacus run: single-pass dispatch skeleton

Shelling out is the design, per SHIFT-REPORT-2026-08-13 section 3: records, acceptance, and evidence chains are explicitly out of scope. Measured finding 3 from the report applies: the launch must carry the bead identity (branch name plus prompt text is the MVP carriage). Test spec: unit tests in src for parsing br ready JSON from a fixture string; integration test that runs real br init plus br create plus br ready --json in a temp dir and exercises the selection code against it. The herdr leg is validated by a live dogfood dispatch, recorded in the bead notes on close.

title: abacus run never reaps the lane: worker pane and workspace persist after completion
description: Observed on the first live dispatch (abacus-geh, 2026-08-13): after the codex worker on lane/abacus-v8s finished and its work was verified and the bead closed, the lane workspace w1P, its worktree checkout, and the idle codex pane persisted indefinitely — the operator had to point it out. At ten concurrent lanes this leaks ten workspaces, ten worktrees, and ten idle agent panes per pass. Fix shape: after the post-settle outcome probe (abacus-zkq introduces it), a verified-complete lane (bead closed) is torn down with herdr worktree remove --workspace <id> — the Lane struct in src/lib.rs already carries workspace_id. The pushed lane branch is the surviving artifact and is never deleted. A lane that did NOT complete (bead open or in_progress) is deliberately left standing for forensics — the pane transcript is the evidence and dies with the pane. Note worktree remove may need --force when the lane holds uncommitted .beads changes, which is currently always per abacus-zyb; the first lane (w1P) was reaped manually with force for exactly this reason. Test spec: unit test the reap decision from the outcome classification (closed reaps, open and in_progress do not); the herdr teardown call is validated live on the next dispatched lane and recorded in notes. Needs abacus-zkq (the outcome probe is what makes reaping safe to decide).

title: abacus run cannot tell a gated lane from a finished one
description: Reproduced live 2026-08-13, first dispatch (see abacus-geh notes). herdr agent prompt --wait settled with agent_status done while the codex worker was actually parked on a startup modal and had processed nothing: no claim on the bead, no commit, no push. abacus run printed the settle JSON and exited 0 — a false success. The settle state alone is not evidence of work. Cheapest evidence-based check per MVP-first, in src/main.rs cmd_run after settle: shell br show <bead-id> --json in the lane checkout (the Lane struct already carries checkout_path) and report the bead status the worker left behind — closed means done, in_progress means it worked but did not finish, still open means the worker never engaged (exit non-zero and say so). Do not build state-machine heuristics over herdr agent states; one br probe distinguishes the three outcomes that matter. Test spec: unit test the outcome classification from bead status; integration test the open-bead path with a fake lane dir holding an initialized br workspace. Needs abacus-5pe understood first only if the fix shape ends up in the launch path; the report-what-the-bead-says probe stands alone.
acceptance_criteria: After settle, abacus run probes br show <bead-id> --json in the lane checkout and reports the outcome from bead status: closed exits 0 as success, in_progress reports incomplete, open reports never-engaged, both non-zero. Unit test covers the three-way classification; integration test covers the open path with a real br workspace in a temp lane dir. Run-1 conditions (worker gated on a modal, settle says done) would exit non-zero.
notes: Corroboration, 2026-08-13: the abacus-v1 orchestrator hit the identical failure independently the same night (herdr done treated as completion while the agent was parked), and the sf reference implementation states the rule outright: either signal is a doorbell, not evidence. Three independent arrivals — this run, v1's, and sf's — make the failure structural, not incidental. The fix shape stands: probe br in the lane for the bead status; never treat runtime agent state as an outcome.

title: Dispatch prompt orders close after push, stranding bead state in the lane
description: Observed on the first successful lane (run 2 of abacus-geh, 2026-08-13). dispatch_prompt in src/lib.rs instructs the worker: commit, push with git push -u origin <branch>, then br close <id>. The close therefore mutates the lane's .beads/issues.jsonl AFTER the branch is pushed, leaving the closed status as an uncommitted working-tree change in the worktree — the pushed branch carries the bead as open, and the main checkout's tracker learns nothing. The codex worker on lane/abacus-v8s reported exactly this: only uncommitted change is .beads/issues.jsonl, produced by the requested post-push br close. Fix shape: reorder the protocol in dispatch_prompt to close the bead before the final commit+push so the branch carries its own completion record (br close, then git add .beads, commit, push). Update the dispatch_prompt unit test in src/lib.rs to assert the ordering (close appears before push in the prompt text). Note the residual gap is claim/close visibility across live lanes generally — that is the known no-tree-claim-coordination hazard, out of scope here; this bead only stops the protocol from stranding state by construction.
acceptance_criteria: dispatch_prompt orders the protocol as br close, then commit including .beads, then push — the pushed lane branch carries the bead closed status. The dispatch_prompt unit test asserts close appears before push in the prompt text. A dispatched lane leaves no uncommitted .beads changes after settling.
notes: Run-3 evidence (zkq lane): the codex worker improvised the correct behavior unprompted — after the instructed push it closed the bead, committed the jsonl as a second commit (7672d49 tracker: close abacus-zkq), and pushed again, so the branch carried its close and the lane reaped with no force. The bead remains valid: the protocol should make this deterministic in dispatch_prompt rather than worker-dependent improvisation. Also note the reap contrast: v8s lane (no close commit) required forced removal; zkq lane (close committed) removed clean.
